page2_img_1.png.title: Gamasutra postmortem screenshot for Pangalore's Knightly Adventure
page2_img_1.png.description: Screenshot of the first page of a Gamasutra postmortem titled “Postmortem: Pangalore’s Knightly Adventure” (by Doyon Kim). The image shows the Gamasutra header and a right-side feature artwork, followed by an introductory paragraph and the two main sections used throughout the paper’s dataset: “What Went Right” (with a numbered item “It’s Two, Two Things in One”) and “What Went Wrong” (with a numbered item “Multiplatform Launch Out of Sync”). The paper cites this figure as an example of the typical multi-page postmortems they analyzed, illustrating the consistent structure (context, what went right/ wrong, and metadata) used to extract categories and themes.

page8_img_1.png.title: Categories cited as “what went wrong” in game postmortems
page8_img_1.png.description: A vertical bar chart (Figure 3) reports the percentage of the analyzed Gamasutra postmortems that list each category as something that went wrong; the y‑axis is “Percentage of Postmortems” and the x‑axis lists 22 specific categories. Bars are color coded by higher‑level groups (maroon = Product, blue = Development, pale yellow = Resources, light blue = Customer‑facing, black = Other). The four most frequently cited pitfalls are Obstacles (≈37%), Schedule (≈25%), Development Process (≈24%), and Game Design (≈22%); several Development bars (Documentation, Team, Testing, Tools) and Resource/Customer bars (Budget, Marketing, Piracy/Licensing) appear at lower but non‑negligible percentages. Because postmortems mention multiple issues, the bars do not sum to 100% — the chart highlights which problem types recur across the 155 postmortems rather than exclusive failure categories.

page7_img_1.png.title: What went right: categories cited in game postmortems
page7_img_1.png.description: A color‑coded bar chart (Figure 2) shows the percentage of the 155 Gamasutra postmortems that mention each topic under “What went right.” The most frequently cited strengths were Game Design (≈50%), Development Process (≈43%), Team (≈40%), and Art (≈39%), while other commonly noted positives include Tools, Testing, Gameplay and Features. Bars are grouped and colored by high‑level category (Product in maroon, Development in blue, Resources in pale yellow, Customer‑Facing in light blue, plus Other in black); values do not sum to 100% because each postmortem lists multiple items. Less frequently listed positives include Documentation, Product Evolution and Hardware, which have very small bars near the bottom of the axis.
